### Also covered by

Fong & Spivak, *Seven Sketches in Compositionality* (CUP, 2019), §4.2.1 Exercise 4.7, printed p. 121 (PDF p. 133) — item `7sketches:4.2.1:ex4.7`. Chapter 4 re-poses the same obligation as its opening warm-up: verify that Boolean implication, given by the truth table of the numbered display (4.6), satisfies the residuation condition of display (4.5) — the conjunction of two truth values lies below a third exactly when the first lies below the implication of the second into the third — i.e. that the two-element order with meet is a closed monoidal preorder with implication as its hom-element.

No new checkbox: this is exactly the checklist item on this issue that asks for `_2` to be shown monoidal closed with the implication hom-element in the biconditional form of Equation (2.80). The only thing the Chapter 4 reading adds is a motivation — this is the closedness that makes the two-element base usable as the enriching base for feasibility relations, and the Chapter 4 profunctor issues depend on this one for it.

### Also covered by

Fong & Spivak, *Seven Sketches in Compositionality* (CUP, 2019), §4.2.1 Exercise 4.4, printed p. 120 (PDF p. 132) — item `7sketches:4.2.1:ex4.4`. Part (1) of the exercise is pictorial (the Hasse diagram of a product preorder) and its ambient is already constructible in tree from `Construction/Opposite.v:106` and `Construction/Product.v:95`. Part (2) is this issue's obligation read at a particular preorder: a monotone map into the booleans is written down and the reader is asked to interpret the fibre over truth as an upper set — here of the product of the opposite of one preorder with another.

- [ ] (from Seven Sketches §4.2.1) Instantiate the classification at a product preorder and draw the consequence the chapter needs: a feasibility relation between two preorders — a Bool-profunctor, as defined by the Seven Sketches §4.2.2 Definition 4.8 issue — is exactly an upper set of the product of the opposite of the source with the target, with the two monotonicity clauses (weakening the source, strengthening the target) read off the product order. State it as a bijection, not as a remark, so the profunctor development can consume it.

### Also covered by

Fong & Spivak, *Seven Sketches in Compositionality* (CUP, 2019), §4.3.2, the unnumbered prose definition of a skeletal quantale immediately preceding Theorem 4.23, printed p. 127 (PDF p. 139) — item `7sketches:4.3.2:def-skeletal-quantale`. Chapter 4 adds a qualifier to the class this issue defines: a preorder is skeletal when mutual comparability forces equality, a quantale is skeletal when its underlying preorder is, and both of the running bases are. Skeletality is not decoration — it is precisely the hypothesis that turns the two mutual inequalities of the profunctor unit and associativity laws into equalities, hence the hypothesis under which V-categories and V-profunctors form a strict category rather than a bicategory.

The skeletal-preorder half already exists in tree, but only as a hypothesis on a specific construction (`Instance/Poset.v:116`'s `Poset` takes an `Antisymmetric` instance) and as two per-instance regression lemmas in a test file (`Test/Poset.v:102,150`); there is no skeletality predicate in the library proper.

- [ ] (from Seven Sketches §4.3.2) Add a `Skeletal` predicate on the quantale class — mutual comparability of two elements implies their equality — as a first-class definition rather than a hypothesis on a construction, prove the two running bases satisfy it (the two-element base by decision, the cost base from antisymmetry of the underlying order), and state the consequence the profunctor development consumes: over a skeletal base, two elements each below the other are equal, so a two-sided inequality proof yields an equality of hom-objects.

### Also covered by

Fong & Spivak, *Seven Sketches in Compositionality* (CUP, 2019), §4.4.3 Exercise 4.48, printed p. 137 (PDF p. 149) — item `7sketches:4.4.3:ex4.48`. Chapter 4 asks for the identification this issue supplies in one direction to be turned into an *exact* one: a monoidal preorder is precisely a monoidal category in which every hom-set has at most one element. The forward leg is this issue's weak presentation (a monoidal structure instantiated at a thin category); the converse is not currently on the checklist.

- [ ] (from Seven Sketches §4.4.3) Prove the converse leg, so the identification is a biconditional: a category whose hom-setoids are subsingletons induces a preorder on its objects (an arrow inhabits the hom-set exactly when the objects are comparable), and a monoidal structure on such a category induces a monoidal-preorder structure on that preorder — monotonicity of the tensor from its functoriality, and the unit, associativity and commutativity clauses from the structural isomorphisms, which are forced to be the unique arrows. Together with the existing forward leg this states that monoidal preorders are exactly the thin monoidal categories.

### Also covered by

Fong & Spivak, *Seven Sketches in Compositionality* (CUP, 2019), §4.4.3 Remark 4.46, printed p. 137 (PDF p. 149) — item `7sketches:4.4.3:remark4.46`. The remark makes two claims. The second is this issue's obligation: by Mac Lane's coherence theorem, symmetric strict monoidal categories are for practical purposes the same as symmetric monoidal ones, which is the licence the book uses to draw wiring diagrams as if the structure were strict. The first is a definitional point the checklist does not yet name.

- [ ] (from Seven Sketches §4.4.3) Add a free-standing symmetric strict monoidal class: the unitors and the associator strict — object-level equalities together with the assertion that each structural isomorphism is the transported identity, as `Structure/Monoidal/Strict.v:52` already does — while the braiding is deliberately left non-strict. Today the only bundlings of strictness with symmetry in tree are `Construction/PROP.v:68` and `Construction/ColouredPROP.v:108`, both of which pin the objects (to the naturals and to lists of colours respectively), and `SymmetricStrict` otherwise occurs only as a functor-level predicate (`Construction/PROP/Universal.v:569`, `Construction/ColouredPROP/Presentation/Universal.v:351`). The class is what the coherence statement quantifies over, and the Seven Sketches §4.4.3 Remark 4.47 issue depends on it.

### Also covered by

Fong & Spivak, *Seven Sketches in Compositionality* (CUP, 2019), §4.4.4 Exercise 4.54, printed p. 139 (PDF p. 151) — item `7sketches:4.4.4:ex4.54`. Read at the cost base, the identity element of an enriched category — constituent (iii) of the chapter's categorified definition — asks what the identity is in a Lawvere metric space, the answer being that the unit lies below the self-distance, i.e. that the distance from a point to itself is zero.

No new checkbox: this issue's checklist already requires the two axioms to be proved as standalone lemmas in the familiar metric form, of which the self-distance statement is one. The only thing the Chapter 4 reading adds is the framing — that the zero self-distance is the *degenerate form of chosen structure*, which is the general phenomenon the Seven Sketches §4.4.4 Remark 4.53 issue proves for an arbitrary thin base.
